summary: Horace Hayman Wilson (1786–1860) was an Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital Medical School. He served the East India Company and Kolkata Mint, and was Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford from 1831 to 1860.

Horace L. Friess (1900–1975) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia and Heidelberg universities. He held posts at Johns Hopkins and Columbia, where he was Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations from 1962 to 1966.
Horst Brinkhaus (born 1945) is an Indologist. He held positions at the University of Münster from around 1978 to 1988 and at Kiel University from circa 1993 to 2011.

Horst Lasic, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of Vienna in 1999. He became a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences in 1995 and a lecturer at Vienna in 1999.

Hosakote Krishna Sastri (1870–1928) was an Indology and archaeology scholar. He served as an epigraphist for the Archaeological Survey of India from around 1904 to 1925 and as Government Epigraphist for India from circa 1920 to 1925.
Hoseok Leigh is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies. He studied under Ha-u Kim and traditional teacher Cheonghwa.

Hoseong Kim (born 1960) is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He founded the Japan Buddhist History Research Institute and served as a professor at Dongguk University as attested in 2011.
Hoshu Mitsuhara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he was recorded as professor in 1982 and professor emeritus in 2004.
Hotetsu Matsumoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who was affiliated with Tohoku University in 1997. He later served as a professor and center director at Shuchiin University, attested in 2026.

Hoyo Watanabe (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University from circa 1952 to 1961. He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor, dean of Buddhist studies, and special honorary professor.
Hozen Seki (1904–1991) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church, attested in 1998.
Hrachia Acharian (1876–1953) was a linguist who studied under Heinrich Hübschmann and Antoine Meillet.

Hrishikesh Terdalkar is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology who earned his PhD at IIT Kanpur under Arnab Bhattacharya, Pralay Manna, and Sowmya Krishnapur. He was affiliated with IIT Kanpur around 2023–2024.

Hsiang-Kuang Chou, a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies, studied under Swami Sivananda. He held posts at the University of Delhi, the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy, the University of Allahabad, and Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy.

Hsiao-Lan Hu is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University. Hu served as an associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy, attested in 2017.

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Tianning Temple, Jiaoshan Buddhist Academy, and under Yinshun. He founded Fo Guang Shan, serving as its abbot from ~1967 to 1985, and taught at Tunghai University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's degree from Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

Hsu Yun (1840–1959) was a Buddhist studies and religious figure who studied under Changkai, Miaolian, and Yaocheng. He co-founded the Buddhist Association of China in 1953, serving as its honorary president.

Hsu-feng Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a master's degree under Huimin at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies and a PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney, attested in 2017.

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Chang Chih and Hsu Yun. He founded Dharma Realm Buddhist Association, Dharma Realm Buddhist University, and the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, and was Abbot of Tathagata Monastery.
